Two objects move toward each due to mutual attraction. The question asks whether the kinetic energy of the system remains constant and if the total linear momentum remains constant despite external forces.

Concept/Solution:
Assertion:
Two objects are moving towards each other due to mutual attraction. The kinetic energy of the system remains constant.

  • When two objects attract each other, such as in gravitational or electrostatic attraction, they move towards each other.
  • In a conservative force system (like gravitational attraction), total mechanical energy (kinetic + potential energy) is conserved, but this does not imply that the kinetic energy remains constant.
  • Hence, the kinetic energy changes as the objects move toward each other.

Reason:
Total linear momentum of the system consisting of both objects remains constant even in the presence of external forces.
  • The total linear momentum of system is conserved if these are no external forces acting on the system.
  • If the objects are only interacting due to their mutual attraction (and no external forces), their total linear momentum would remain constant.
  • However, if external force are acting on the system, the linear momentum could change.
